Unfortunately, It is complicated to resolve with a regular adblock rule because the website is being protected by service of Ad-Shield that is an anti-adblock company.

## Userscript Installation
Please block Ad-Shield advertisement by installing [tinyShield userscript](https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield).
Please check its installation guideline written in English by visiting [this URL](https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield/blob/main/README.md).

If you can understand Korean language, please refer https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield/blob/main/README.ko.md.

New change of tinyShield's build script for Apple Safari Extension user (made at 2026 Apr 21) is available.

## Still Have a Problem?
An issue is occurred when the userscript is applied, please report to [this issue tracker](https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield/issues).

### Issue URL (Anti Adblock Script) [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/faa-ground-stop-canceled-flights-travelers-what-we-know/](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.cbsnews.com%2Fnews%2Ffaa-ground-stop-canceled-flights-travelers-what-we-know%2F) ### Comment > ### Issue Description > Anti-adblock wall on `cbsnews.com` via Admiral First-Party Proxy. > > * **A/B Test Behavior:** Clean/Incognito sessions are served an inescapable hard wall with no dismiss link and page scrolling locked (`overflow: hidden`). Some regular sessions occasionally receive a variant with a delayed *"I'll fix it next time"* dismiss button. > * **Consent Requirement:** Only triggers after OneTrust (`cbsoptanon`) allows targeting/advertising cookies (`cmp.ot.targetingAllowed`). > > ### Proxied Admiral Script URLs Observed > * `https://silkyslumber.com/static/kmxtcpfvq/q1zxupa.js` > * `https://topicspin.com/static/k6vi91qgp/siqqoqasp4mu874ckh6569s5n2uum.js` > > ### Inline Bootstrap & Obfuscation Details > * Admiral's inline loader is wrapped in `loadAdmiralScript()` and invoked asynchronously inside `cbsoptanon.onScriptsReady` $\rightarrow$ `cmp.ot.targetingAllowed`. > * Because `loadAdmiralScript()` runs asynchronously after `document.currentScript` is `null`, inline scriptlets hooking `document.createElement` do not catch it. > * Evades generic Admiral signatures by aliasing `decodeURI` (`D(D(Y))`) and double-encoding `'admiral'` (`%25%36%31%64m%25%36%39%25%37%32%2561%6C`). > * Static Admiral Property ID in inline script: `QS01RDlDQzI1QTgyQ0FFMzUwNTQ5RkMwQUMtMg` > > ### Suggested / Verified Fix > Aborting synchronously when `loadAdmiralScript` is registered with `cbsoptanon.onScriptsReady` blocks Admiral before any proxied scripts are fetched: > ```adblock > cbsnews.com#%#//scriptlet('abort-current-inline-script', 'cbsoptanon.onScriptsReady', 'loadAdmiralScript') > ``` ``` Username: @SpoiledSneeze ``` ### Screenshots

Some regular sessions occasionally receive a variant with a delayed *"I'll fix it next time"* dismiss button. > * **Consent Requirement:** Only triggers after OneTrust (`cbsoptanon`) allows targeting/advertising cookies (`cmp.ot.targetingAllowed`). > > ### Proxied Admiral Script URLs Observed > * `https://silkyslumber.com/static/kmxtcpfvq/q1zxupa.js` > * `https://topicspin.com/static/k6vi91qgp/siqqoqasp4mu874ckh6569s5n2uum.js` > > ### Inline Bootstrap & Obfuscation Details > * Admiral's inline loader is wrapped in `loadAdmiralScript()` and invoked asynchronously inside `cbsoptanon.onScriptsReady` $\rightarrow$ `cmp.ot.targetingAllowed`. > * Because `loadAdmiralScript()` runs asynchronously after `document.currentScript` is `null`, inline scriptlets hooking `document.createElement` do not catch it. > * Evades generic Admiral signatures by aliasing `decodeURI` (`D(D(Y))`) and double-encoding `'admiral'` (`%25%36%31%64m%25%36%39%25%37%32%2561%6C`). > * Static Admiral Property ID in inline script: `QS01RDlDQzI1QTgyQ0FFMzUwNTQ5RkMwQUMtMg` > > ### Suggested / Verified Fix > Aborting synchronously when `loadAdmiralScript` is registered with `cbsoptanon.onScriptsReady` blocks Admiral before any proxied scripts are fetched: > ```adblock > cbsnews.com#%#//scriptlet('abort-current-inline-script', 'cbsoptanon.onScriptsReady', 'loadAdmiralScript') > ``` ``` Username: @SpoiledSneeze ``` ### Screenshots

Indeterminate — The slate.com anti-adblock wall ("We need to talk about your adblocker") never rendered in the runner. Its element is still served as dialog.slate-modal.blocker-intercept__standard, which the published slate.com#⁠$?#⁠dialog.blocker-intercept rule no longer matches. I recommend a maintainer update that selector (candidate in the Popups antiadblock file); apply_rule could not verify it and returned baseline_symptom_absent.

`slate.com#$?#dialog.blocker-intercept__standard { remove: true; }`

AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/antiadblock.txt

### Issue URL (Anti Adblock Script) [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/faa-ground-stop-canceled-flights-travelers-what-we-know/](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.cbsnews.com%2Fnews%2Ffaa-ground-stop-canceled-flights-travelers-what-we-know%2F) ### Comment > ### Issue Description > Anti-adblock wall on `cbsnews.com` via Admiral First-Party Proxy. > > * **A/B Test Behavior:** Clean/Incognito sessions are served an inescapable hard wall with no dismiss link and page scrolling locked (`overflow: hidden`). Some regular sessions occasionally receive a variant with a delayed *"I'll fix it next time"* dismiss button. > * **Consent Requirement:** Only triggers after OneTrust (`cbsoptanon`) allows targeting/advertising cookies (`cmp.ot.targetingAllowed`). > > ### Proxied Admiral Script URLs Observed > * `https://silkyslumber.com/static/kmxtcpfvq/q1zxupa.js` > * `https://topicspin.com/static/k6vi91qgp/siqqoqasp4mu874ckh6569s5n2uum.js` > > ### Inline Bootstrap & Obfuscation Details > * Admiral's inline loader is wrapped in `loadAdmiralScript()` and invoked asynchronously inside `cbsoptanon.onScriptsReady` $\rightarrow$ `cmp.ot.targetingAllowed`. > * Because `loadAdmiralScript()` runs asynchronously after `document.currentScript` is `null`, inline scriptlets hooking `document.createElement` do not catch it. > * Evades generic Admiral signatures by aliasing `decodeURI` (`D(D(Y))`) and double-encoding `'admiral'` (`%25%36%31%64m%25%36%39%25%37%32%2561%6C`). > * Static Admiral Property ID in inline script: `QS01RDlDQzI1QTgyQ0FFMzUwNTQ5RkMwQUMtMg` > > ### Suggested / Verified Fix > Aborting synchronously when `loadAdmiralScript` is registered with `cbsoptanon.onScriptsReady` blocks Admiral before any proxied scripts are fetched: > ```adblock > cbsnews.com#%#//scriptlet('abort-current-inline-script', 'cbsoptanon.onScriptsReady', 'loadAdmiralScript') > ``` ``` Username: @SpoiledSneeze ``` ### Screenshots

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"e3567947956790009277827b10abf7c49107cebf342e9412730672d16d081af2"} -->
The filter policy recommends closing without a rule

## Reproduced symptom

The reported URL is a SquadBeyond-delivered 「PR」 advertorial on the advertiser's own subdomain, where all advertising (the Potenza article creatives and the popin to store.yakuin-organic.co.jp) is the site operator's own first-party promotion, and the report names no publisher page for a third-party ad placement. The only rule that removed the graphic creatives, ||mysquadbeyond.com^$third-party, was rejected by the bound review for a regressed page, so per the filter policy's "first-party ads:⁠ no rule" I recommend closing.

## Policy rationale

Run instruction filter policy:⁠ "The site's own advertising (first-party ads):⁠ no rule; recommend closing." Every advertisement observed on the reported site promotes the site operator's own product, so the reported defect falls under this rule. Linked filter policy (KnowledgeBase filter-policy.md, Limitations and exceptions):⁠ "The site's own advertising should not be deliberately blocked." A rule that removes these creatives on the reported site deliberately blocks that site's own advertising. The reachable page is the ad's own destination, not a page carrying a third-party ad placement:⁠ the report names no publisher page, so no third-party ad unit could be located or verified. The only rule tried that stopped the reported creatives (||mysquadbeyond.com^$third-party, a block of the advertorial delivery platform) also stripped all 35 media elements from the page and was rejected by the bound vision review for a regressed page with observed damage, so no policy-compliant verified rule exists.

## Artifacts

issue.body:
### Issue URL (Incorrect Blocking)
[https://kingpindesigns.com/](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Fkingpindesigns.com%2F)

### Comment
> **kingpindesigns.com** and all of its subdomains are blocked by AdGuard DNS as a "Dangerous website" (phishing/malicious). This is a false positive.
> 
> Affected names include:
> - kingpindesigns.com
> - www.kingpindesigns.com
> - nrd.kingpindesigns.com
> - nrd.boards.kingpindesigns.com
> 
> **Steps to reproduce**
> 1. Set the device's DNS to AdGuard DNS Default (94.140.14.14).
> 2. Open https://kingpindesigns.com.
> 3. The AdGuard "Access blocked: Dangerous website" page is shown. With any other DNS, the site loads normally.
> 
> AdGuard DNS answers 94.140.14.33 (the block server) for every name on the domain. Cloudflare, Quad9, OpenDNS, CleanBrowsing and Google DNS answer normally, and Google Safe Browsing reports "No unsafe content found."
> 
> **About the domain**
> The domain belongs to Kingpin Designs LLC, a small software business that builds menu boards, staff dashboards and websites for roller rinks and family entertainment centers. The site hosts no phishing, malware, ads or tracking. It is hosted on Cloudflare with valid certificates. If the domain was misused before we registered it, that was a previous owner.
> 
> Please remove kingpindesigns.com and its subdomains from the phishing/malicious list. Thank you.

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"086e3f93b57c93916c44b62ea022efb27a33ad9b6df553798b18d3096475a6c9"} -->
The filter policy leaves this report to a maintainer

## Reproduced symptom

The anti-adblock dialog from the reporter's screenshot never appears on the reported weather.com page under the current lists — complete full-page vision finds it absent and the site's own interstitial mount point (`#MW_Interstitial`) stays empty — because the existing weather.com scriptlet group in the Popups filter is applied. The run instruction allows a rule for a non-German anti-adblock wall only once captured requests show the detector script, and none was captured, so a maintainer must decide, including whether the scriptlet fix reaches AdGuard Mini for Android.

## Policy rationale

Run instruction, Filter policy:⁠ "Any other anti-adblock wall:⁠ write a rule only once the page's requests the agent captured show the detector script; without it, hand the report to a maintainer." This wall is not German (Traditional Chinese modal on weather.com), so the German no-rule exception does not apply, and the captured requests (artifact:⁠har:⁠ff00c735-1d8b-447f-b08e-0cf1eab41713) show no detector script that renders the wall — the detector never fires on the filtered baseline. Run instruction, Filter policy, German anti-adblock walls:⁠ "This covers only a German site's wall or popup that detects the ad blocker ... A page in German is not enough, and the reporter's choice of 'anti-adblock' as the problem type is not evidence" — so the language-specific exception cannot be used to close this report. Run instruction, Maintainer rules / Anti-adblock popups:⁠ a cosmetic hide is allowed only for a popup that is actually produced; here the wall's mount point (`#MW_Interstitial`, `[data-testid="MW_Interstitial"]`) is present but empty and 0x0 on the baseline, so no element of the complaint was observed to hide or to validate. Routing guidance for mobile products:⁠ the reporter runs AdGuard Mini for Android in Samsung Browser while evidence was collected through the AdGuard CLI proxy; the existing weather.com fix is the `#%#//scriptlet(...)` group in AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/antiadblock.txt, and whether that execution model reaches the reported mobile product is an unverified hypothesis for a maintainer's product decision, not something a new filter rule can settle.

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"48829ffa58dd548b012cee76ff5861575221f145a58188c5cb62582925d129dc"} -->
The filter policy leaves this report to a maintainer

## Reproduced symptom

The weeklyOSM page loads and renders fully with no anti-adblock wall, ad or detector:⁠ the CLI-filtered baseline applied zero rules and the network log has only first-party weeklyosm.eu requests, so the reporter's blank-page screenshot is not reproducible. No rule can be written — the run instruction forbids an anti-adblock rule without a captured detector script and hands such reports to a maintainer, so this only recommends closing for a maintainer's decision.

## Policy rationale

Run instruction, Filter policy:⁠ "Any other anti-adblock wall:⁠ write a rule only once the page's requests the agent captured show the detector script; without it, hand the report to a maintainer." The issue is labelled 'T:⁠ Anti Adblock Script', but no detector script, no ad-recovery loader and no third-party host appears among the 80 captured requests, so the policy forbids generating an anti-adblock rule and requires a maintainer handoff. Run instruction, Filter policy:⁠ "The site's own advertising (first-party ads):⁠ no rule; recommend closing." The page carries no advertising of any kind that a rule could target (see evidence). Run instruction:⁠ "The agent never closes an issue." This outcome only recommends closing on the policy basis above; the final decision stays with a maintainer.

The reported defect was not reproduced

## Reproduced symptom

Not reproduced — With the reporter's own filter selection the locked AdGuard extension loads dailyorbs.com and its puzzle page (including the screenshot's /doctor-speak-iv address) in full, full-page vision finds the blank dark page absent, and the only rules acting — the ad-rail hide and the fuse.js ad-script block — remove no page content, so no filter rule is needed and a maintainer may close. The reporter's Firefox MV2 extension cannot be exercised in this run, so that platform difference is noted rather than proven.

## Executor and version
